title: Beer and Free Lunches
coreMove: Remove the audience or sequence pressure so the real preference can surface cheaply.
sourcePressure: The source closes on public choice, beer ordering, and the idea that predictable irrationality creates cheap design fixes that recover better preferences.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says people conform; the precise lesson is that visibility and sequence contaminate preference revelation, and low-cost design can clean it up.

hook: The room orders before you do
The beer is not just beer

exampleSpecs.domain: bookstore staff choosing front-window picks aloud
exampleSpecs.audience: a store manager trying to learn what books staff genuinely recommend
exampleSpecs.stakes: filling the window with impressive picks rather than books staff can hand-sell well
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after switching from aloud nominations to sealed shelf cards, the manager sees more varied picks and stronger sales notes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sealed shelf cards stacked beside an empty bookstore window display

exampleSpecs.audience: a station captain trying to choose meals firefighters will actually eat
exampleSpecs.stakes: public bravado pushing spicy or heavy meals that half the crew avoids
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain replaces shouted meal votes with folded slips before the first senior firefighter can set the tone
exampleSpecs.firstImage: folded meal slips in a stainless pan beside a firehouse duty board

exampleSpecs.audience: teen dancers choosing songs while peers are watching
exampleSpecs.stakes: selecting trendy music that weakens performance because no one wants to seem uncool
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the instructor has dancers rank songs privately, then reveals that the strongest practice scores match the private favorite
exampleSpecs.firstImage: song title slips scattered on a sprung studio floor

exampleSpecs.domain: software incident retrospective choosing root causes
exampleSpecs.audience: an engineering manager who wants honest prioritization after an outage
exampleSpecs.stakes: engineers naming socially safe causes once senior staff speak first
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager collects anonymous root-cause cards before anyone talks, then compares them with the spoken discussion
exampleSpecs.firstImage: anonymous root-cause cards beside a red incident timeline on a monitor

exampleSpecs.domain: craft brewery tasting flight order forms
exampleSpecs.audience: a taproom owner trying to learn real customer preference among experimental beers
exampleSpecs.stakes: customers choosing the bold-sounding beer to look adventurous when ordering aloud
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the owner lets half the room order by private numbered cards and compares reorder rates with the aloud-order group
exampleSpecs.firstImage: numbered tasting cards lined beside small flight glasses on a wooden bar

exampleSpecs.audience: a school principal trying to learn what repairs families most value
exampleSpecs.stakes: visible hands favoring prestigious additions while basic safety repairs lose
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the principal switches from show-of-hands to private ranked ballots and the cracked rubber surface rises above the new mural
exampleSpecs.firstImage: ranked ballots tucked under a photo of a cracked playground surface

skillTargets: identify when public sequence contaminates preference
evaluate whether a free-lunch intervention improves signal without coercion

tryThisNowSpec: For one group decision this week, collect first preferences privately before discussion starts, then compare the private signal with the public conversation.
